extracted.intended_audience: general readers of humorous social essays (Victorian-era)
extracted.subtask_description: Lightly comic, observational essays giving social commentary, anecdote, and practical (often ironic) advice on human habits and feelings. The tone is conversational, wry, and aimed at general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evening-specific melancholy
rubrics_metrics.description: “By the way, it never does come except in the evening.” Melancholy (the 'blues') is described as an evening phenomenon: dark, pensive, associated with twilight and night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symptoms and behaviours: brooding in the evening, feeling worthless, contrasting imagined future regard with present neglect, becoming savage then restrained by bedtime, tossing and changing clothes in bed, bad dreams, waking late. Contrast with daytime reactions (anger, swearing, furniture-smashing). The essayist treats the timing (evening) as characteristic and diagnostic of this mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melancholy stems from remembered sorrow not current trouble
rubrics_metrics.description: “As a rule, it is not trouble that makes us melancholy. The actuality is too stern a thing for sentiment.” Melancholy is fed by memory and the pleasurable habit of dwelling on past sorrow rather than by present misfortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive note: real misery lacks the luxury of sentiment; when people keep sorrow 'green' it often becomes a pleasure. Examples: old ladies cherishing tiny shoes/locks as pleasant recollection; tears can be as sweet as laughter to some natures. Use this to explain why people luxuriate in regret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of feminine sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: “I would not for a moment sneer at anything that helps to keep hearts tender... No, no, ladies dear, be always sentimental and soft-hearted.” The author defends women's sentimentality as socially and emotionally valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mock sentiment that keeps hearts tender; sentiment in women is likened to 'soothing butter' to men's coarse bread. The passage recommends allowing and respecting this mode of enjoyment rather than deriding it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature regret = healed grief
rubrics_metrics.description: “I am glad when I see Regret walked with as a friend... Time has laid his healing hand upon the wound when we can look back upon the pain...and no bitterness or despair rises in our hearts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for healthy mourning: one can recall past pain without bitterness; remembrance mingles pleasure and pity. Cited examples (Colonel Newcome, Tom and Maggie Tulliver) illustrate dignified, reconciled remembrance as a positive state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearances and concealment of poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: “Being poor is a mere trifle. It is being known to be poor that is the sting... Appearances are everything, so far as human opinion goes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social rule: conceal visible signs of poverty to avoid scorn. The embarrassed, seedy-looking man avoids acquaintances and prefers to be forgotten. Practical implication: shame of being known poor is a greater social injury than poverty itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graceful pawning (composure when revealing need)
rubrics_metrics.description: “True ease in pawning comes from art, not chance.” The experienced, hard-up person handles pawning with calm composure; the novice behaves awkwardly and attracts attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast behaviors: the practiced customer enters with assurance and businesslike manner; the novice hangs about, tries to appear as a buyer, speaks inaudibly, stammers, forgets details, and exits humiliated. Advice implied: practice, composure, and treating such transactions as routine reduce the social sting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flattery as universal social lubricant
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ay, ay, vanity is truly the motive-power that moves humanity, and it is flattery that greases the wheels.” Flattery is presented as the practical method to win affection, respect, and cooperation from everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical guidance: flatter broadly—high and low, rich and poor, silly and wise. Compliment people on virtues and even on things they lack. Flattery should be adapted to the target: some accept heavy-handed praise, others need delicate suggestion, some only swallow praise wrapped as an insult, and some respond to praise relayed through a third party. Examples illustrate adapting style (e.g., the man who 'hates flattery' can be flattered about his disdain for it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor flattery to the listener (methods/examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different people require different modes of flattery: trowel-on, delicate suggestion, insult-wrapped praise, or third-party endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific modes described: (a) 'laid on with a trowel'—obvious, plentiful praise; (b) delicate suggestion—imply rather than state; (c) wrapped insult—praise disguised as banter ('Oh, you are a perfect fool, you are'); (d) relayed praise—tell a trusted friend that you think highly of the target so they hear it second-hand. Pick method to match sensibilities and ensure B is reliable when using third-party route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vanity constructively — be vain of noble things
rubrics_metrics.description: “After all, vanity is as much a virtue as a vice... Let us be vain, not of our trousers and hair, but of brave hearts and working hands, of truth, of purity, of nobility.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative prescription: accept that vanity motivates action (ambition as 'vanity ennobled') and redirect it toward worthy ends. Encourage pride in virtue and achievement rather than mere outward show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winning animals' (especially cats') favour requires tailored approach
rubrics_metrics.description: “To win the approbation of a cat you must mind what you are about and work your way carefully... begin by saying, 'Poor pussy.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps for cats: use soothing, slightly nonsensical sympathy ('did 'ums'), then stroke and pat; expect claws as part of the bargain. Contrast with dogs: dogs are openly friendly and accept rough handling, cats require delicate, flattering approaches.
